The Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 84, verses 16–21:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[16–21] ﴿So I swear by the twilight﴾ ﴿and the night and what it envelops﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 17] ﴿and the moon when it becomes full﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 18] ﴿You will surely embark from state to state﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 19] ﴿So what is wrong with them that they do not believe?﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 20] ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate?﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 21]

(p-6110) ﴿So I swear by the twilight﴾: it is the redness in the horizon on the side of the sunset. ﴿And the night and what it envelops﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 17]: i.e., what it gathers and draws together of what rests and becomes still in it, of living creatures that fly or crawl by day. Thus said Ibn Jarir. But the more evident view is that it refers to all things, since the night encompasses them all, so that it is as if He swore by all created beings, as He said: ﴿So I swear by what you see﴾ [al-Haqqah: 38] ﴿and what you do not see﴾ [al-Haqqah: 39]. ﴿And the moon when it becomes full﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 18]: i.e., when it gathers, its light is complete and it becomes perfect. ﴿You will surely embark from state to state﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 19]: i.e., one condition after another. What is meant by the first condition is the raising up for the recompense for deeds, and by the second the first life. In this is an indication of the correspondence of each to its counterpart, for the second life resembles the first and matches it in terms of sensation, perception, pain and pleasure, even if its reality is hidden. It is also permitted that "ṭabaqan" is the plural of "ṭabaqah," which means a rank, i.e., you will surely ride severe ranks, passing beyond ranks and levels, and stages arranged by death and what follows it from the abode of resurrection and rising again.

Al-Shihab said: "ṭabaq" literally means that which corresponds to another in general, and then it was specialized to what has been mentioned, namely a corresponding condition, or successive degrees of severity.

"ʿan" is for passing beyond, or in the sense of "after." Being after and passing beyond are close in meaning, but the latter is more evident. ﴿So what is wrong with them that they do not believe?﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 20]: i.e., in this discourse, and He had established for them the proof for monotheism and the resurrection.

﴿And when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate?﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 21]: i.e., they do not submit, nor humble themselves, nor yield.

In (al-Iklil) it is said: This has been cited as evidence for the legislated status of the prostration of recitation.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 84, verses 22–25:

The discussion of His saying, the Exalted:

[22–25] ﴿Nay, those who disbelieve deny it.﴾ ﴿And Allah is most knowing of what they conceal.﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 23] (p. 6111) ﴿So give them tidings of a painful punishment.﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 24] ﴿Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds; theirs is a reward never to be cut off.﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 25]

﴿Nay, those who disbelieve deny it﴾, i.e., they deny the signs of Allah and His revelation that clarifies what has been mentioned of the states of the Resurrection and its terrors, despite the establishment of the grounds that necessitate its affirmation. The particle "bal" (nay, rather) here is an idrab (a turning away from a previous statement) from an omitted clause, whose sense—as the Imam [al-Razi] said—is: Do not suppose that the striking of the Qur'an has not broken the locks of their hearts, nor that its voice has failed to reach the depths of their consciences. Rather, it has indeed reached them and persuaded them in what it reached; but obstinacy is what prevents them from faith and holds them back from submission. The source of denial is therefore not any deficiency in the proof, but the negligence of the one who seeks guidance and his turning away from its guidance. Thus the turning away points to an omitted statement in speech that is indicated by what precedes and what follows.

﴿And Allah is most knowing of what they conceal﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 23], i.e., of what they keep hidden in their breasts concerning the truth of the revelation, even if they conceal it out of obstinacy; or of what they harbor of rebellion and deceit, and He will requite them for it. Therefore He said: ﴿So give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 24], i.e., as a recompense for their denial, their turning away, and their rebellion.

﴿Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds; theirs is a reward never to be cut off﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 25], i.e., one that is not interrupted, or one that is not bestowed upon them as a favor (la yumannu bihi 'alayhim). The exception is either disjunctive (munqati') or conjunctive (muttasil), on the basis that by "those who believe" is meant those among them who embraced Islam, and they believed with respect to what has passed, or it carries the sense of "they believe." That it is disjunctive is more apparent, given the coming of "theirs is a reward" without a fa' (the particle of consequence). And Allah knows best.
